SpaceProperties.context.title: Properties tabs
SpaceProperties.context.body: Each icon down the left edge of the Properties editor opens a different drawer of settings: render, output, scene, world, then everything about the selected object (object, modifiers, particles, physics, constraints, data, materials).
SpaceProperties.context.try: Hover each tab and read its tooltip. The tabs change depending on what's selected.

Object.parent.title: Parent
Object.parent.body: The object this one follows. Move, rotate, or scale the parent and the child comes along, keeping its offset. Like a moon around a planet.
Object.parent.shortcut: Ctrl+P to parent (last selected becomes parent), Alt+P to clear

OBJECT_OT_parent_set.title: Set Parent
OBJECT_OT_parent_set.body: Makes the active object (the last one you clicked) the parent of the other selected objects.

OBJECT_OT_move_to_collection.title: Move to Collection
OBJECT_OT_move_to_collection.body: Files the selected objects into a collection, a folder for objects. Collections can be hidden, excluded from renders, or linked into other files all at once.

OBJECT_OT_hide_view_set.title: Hide
OBJECT_OT_hide_view_set.body: Hides the selected objects in the viewport. They still exist and still render unless you also turn off rendering.
OBJECT_OT_hide_view_set.shortcut: H hides selected, Shift+H hides everything else, Alt+H reveals all

OBJECT_OT_hide_view_clear.title: Reveal Hidden
OBJECT_OT_hide_view_clear.body: Brings back every object you hid in the viewport.

OBJECT_OT_shade_smooth.title: Shade Smooth
OBJECT_OT_shade_smooth.body: Blends the lighting across faces so a low-poly shape looks rounded. It doesn't add geometry; it only changes how light reads the surface.
OBJECT_OT_shade_smooth.try: Pair it with a Subdivision Surface modifier for silky results.

OBJECT_OT_modifier_add.title: Add Modifier
OBJECT_OT_modifier_add.body: Adds a modifier: a non-destructive recipe that changes the shape (or more) every time Blender redraws, without touching the real mesh until you apply it.

OBJECT_OT_modifier_apply.title: Apply Modifier
OBJECT_OT_modifier_apply.body: Bakes the modifier's result into real geometry and removes the recipe. Handy, but final.
OBJECT_OT_modifier_apply.shortcut: Ctrl+A while hovering the modifier panel

SubsurfModifier.levels.title: Subdivision Levels (Viewport)
SubsurfModifier.levels.body: How many times each face is split and smoothed in the viewport. Every level roughly quadruples the face count, so 2 or 3 is plenty while you work.
SubsurfModifier.levels.shortcut: Ctrl+1, Ctrl+2, Ctrl+3 in Object Mode adds Subdivision at that level

SubsurfModifier.render_levels.title: Subdivision Levels (Render)
SubsurfModifier.render_levels.body: The subdivision level used in final renders. It can be higher than the viewport level, since renders happen once.

Modifier.show_viewport.title: Show in Viewport
Modifier.show_viewport.body: Turns the modifier's effect on or off in the viewport without deleting it. Great for comparing before and after, or keeping a heavy scene snappy.

Modifier.show_render.title: Show in Render
Modifier.show_render.body: Turns the modifier on or off for final renders.

ArrayModifier.count.title: Array Count
ArrayModifier.count.body: How many copies the Array makes, including the original.

ArrayModifier.relative_offset_displace.title: Relative Offset
ArrayModifier.relative_offset_displace.body: How far apart the copies are, measured in multiples of the object's own size. 1 means touching, 1.5 leaves a half-size gap. Each axis is separate, so X and Y make rows and columns.

BevelModifier.width.title: Bevel Amount
BevelModifier.width.body: How wide the bevel cuts into each sharp edge.

BevelModifier.segments.title: Bevel Segments
BevelModifier.segments.body: How many steps the bevel uses. 1 is a flat chamfer, 3 or more starts to look round.

WireframeModifier.thickness.title: Wireframe Thickness
WireframeModifier.thickness.body: How thick each beam is when the Wireframe modifier turns edges into struts.

ToolSettings.mesh_select_mode.title: Select Mode
ToolSettings.mesh_select_mode.body: What a click grabs in Edit Mode: vertices (points), edges (lines), or faces (surfaces). Shift-click to combine modes.

tool:builtin.extrude_region.title: Extrude Region
tool:builtin.extrude_region.body: Pulls the selection outward, building new walls behind it. The single most used modeling tool.

tool:builtin.inset_faces.title: Inset Faces
tool:builtin.inset_faces.body: Shrinks a face inward and fills the border with a ring of new faces. A frame within a frame, perfect before an extrude.

tool:builtin.bevel.title: Bevel
tool:builtin.bevel.body: Rounds off sharp edges or corners. Scroll the wheel while dragging for more segments.
tool:builtin.bevel.shortcut: Ctrl+B for edges, Ctrl+Shift+B for vertices

tool:builtin.loop_cut.title: Loop Cut
tool:builtin.loop_cut.body: Slices a new ring of edges all the way around a shape, giving you more geometry exactly where you need it.

tool:builtin.knife.title: Knife
tool:builtin.knife.body: Draw new cuts across faces by clicking points. Enter to confirm, Esc to cancel.

MESH_OT_merge.title: Merge
MESH_OT_merge.body: Melts selected vertices into one. At Center puts the result in the middle; By Distance cleans up doubles that sit on top of each other.

MESH_OT_delete.title: Delete
MESH_OT_delete.body: Removes vertices, edges, or faces. Deleting faces leaves the edges around the hole; Dissolve removes geometry while keeping the surface closed.
MESH_OT_delete.shortcut: X or Delete in Edit Mode

MATERIAL_OT_new.title: New Material
MATERIAL_OT_new.body: Creates a fresh material and puts it in the selected slot. A material decides color, shine, metalness, transparency and more.

OBJECT_OT_material_slot_add.title: Add Material Slot
OBJECT_OT_material_slot_add.body: Adds an empty slot so one object can wear more than one material. Fill it with New, then Assign it to faces in Edit Mode.

OBJECT_OT_material_slot_assign.title: Assign Material
OBJECT_OT_material_slot_assign.body: Paints the selected faces (in Edit Mode) with the material in the highlighted slot.

Material.name.title: Material Name
Material.name.body: What this material is called. Materials are shared between objects, so a good name (BrushedSteel, not Material.014) saves a lot of hunting.

Light.energy.title: Light Power
Light.energy.body: How bright the light is, in watts. Area and point lights often need hundreds or thousands of watts; the Sun uses a strength in a different unit, so small numbers like 3 to 5 are typical.

Light.color.title: Light Color
Light.color.body: The tint of the light. Warm oranges feel like late afternoon, cool blues like moonlight or shade.

AreaLight.size.title: Area Light Size
AreaLight.size.body: How big the glowing panel is. Bigger lights make softer shadows with blurrier edges, exactly like a photographer's softbox.

AreaLight.shape.title: Area Light Shape
AreaLight.shape.body: Square, rectangle, disk, or ellipse. Changes the shape of the glow and of reflections in shiny surfaces.

Camera.lens.title: Focal Length
Camera.lens.body: Like swapping lenses on a real camera. Low numbers (18 to 24 mm) are wide and dramatic, 50 mm feels natural, 85 mm and up flatten faces flatteringly.

CameraDOFSettings.use_dof.title: Depth of Field
CameraDOFSettings.use_dof.body: Blurs everything that isn't at the focus distance, like a real lens. Pick a Focus Object so the camera always stays sharp on it.

CameraDOFSettings.aperture_fstop.title: F-Stop
CameraDOFSettings.aperture_fstop.body: How strong the blur is. Low numbers (1.4, 2) mean dreamy blur; high numbers (8, 16) keep everything sharp.

SpaceView3D.lock_camera.title: Lock Camera to View
SpaceView3D.lock_camera.body: While on, navigating in camera view moves the camera itself. Turn it on to frame a shot by hand, then off so you don't bump it.

VIEW3D_OT_view_camera.title: Camera View
VIEW3D_OT_view_camera.body: Look through the scene's active camera: exactly what a render will show.

VIEW3D_OT_camera_to_view.title: Align Camera to View
VIEW3D_OT_camera_to_view.body: Moves the active camera to exactly where you're looking from right now.

RenderSettings.engine.title: Render Engine
RenderSettings.engine.body: Which renderer draws the final image. EEVEE is fast and great for most work, Cycles traces real light paths for accuracy, Workbench is a quick flat preview.

RenderSettings.resolution_percentage.title: Resolution %
RenderSettings.resolution_percentage.body: Renders at a percentage of the full size. 50% renders about four times faster, perfect while testing.

RENDER_OT_render.title: Render Image
RENDER_OT_render.body: Renders a still picture from the active camera and opens it in a render window. Save it from that window's Image menu.

Scene.frame_current.title: Current Frame
Scene.frame_current.body: Where the playhead sits in time. Change it to jump around your animation.

Scene.frame_end.title: End Frame
Scene.frame_end.body: The last frame of the animation. Playback loops back to Start when it reaches here.

ANIM_OT_keyframe_insert_menu.title: Insert Keyframe
ANIM_OT_keyframe_insert_menu.body: Records the current value (location, rotation, scale and more) at the current frame. Blender animates smoothly between keyframes.

SCREEN_OT_animation_play.title: Play Animation
SCREEN_OT_animation_play.body: Plays the animation in the viewport. Press again to pause; Esc stops and returns to where you started.

WM_OT_save_mainfile.title: Save
WM_OT_save_mainfile.body: Saves the .blend file. Blender also keeps autosaves and a .blend1 backup of the previous save, just in case.

area.OUTLINER.title: Outliner
area.OUTLINER.body: A list of everything in the scene, organized in collections and parent-child trees. Click names to select, double-click to rename, use the eye to hide.
area.OUTLINER.try: Click the little arrow beside an object to see what's inside it: mesh data, materials, modifiers.

area.PROPERTIES.title: Properties Editor
area.PROPERTIES.body: Every setting of the scene and the selected object, sorted into tabs down the left edge.
area.PROPERTIES.try: Select different kinds of objects (a light, a camera, a mesh) and watch the tabs change.

area.NODE_EDITOR.title: Node Editor
area.NODE_EDITOR.body: Materials, geometry and compositing drawn as boxes and wires. Data flows left to right into the output on the far right.
area.NODE_EDITOR.shortcut: Shift+A adds nodes, Ctrl+Right-drag cuts wires, Home frames everything

area.DOPESHEET_EDITOR.title: Timeline
area.DOPESHEET_EDITOR.body: Time, laid out left to right. Diamonds are keyframes, the blue line is the current frame, and the controls play, stop and jump.
area.DOPESHEET_EDITOR.shortcut: Space plays, Left/Right arrows step frames
